posts.text:
Quick reference: SCCA Solo number requirements so you don't get bounced at tech.

Here's what the rulebook actually says:

- Numbers must be minimum 8" tall
- Minimum stroke width of 1.25"
- Must contrast with car body color
- Required on BOTH sides of the car
- Class letters required — same rules on size and contrast
- Novice drivers need an "X" after their number

Common mistakes we see:
1. Numbers that are technically 8" but the font makes them hard to read from a distance. Block fonts are your friend.
2. White numbers on silver cars. Tech will send you back.
3. Tape numbers that are peeling by run 3. Just get vinyl.

We cut all our autocross kits to meet these specs out of the box. No guessing.

Full kits: https://blueridgecustomco.com/racing-packages.html

posts.text:
Vinyl numbers vs magnetic numbers — honest breakdown from someone who's used both.

VINYL (permanent stick-on):
+ Cheapest option
+ Won't fly off at any speed
+ Clean look, sits flush with the body
- Semi-permanent — removing them can be annoying
- Can leave adhesive residue if cheap vinyl is used
- Not great if you change numbers between orgs

MAGNETIC:
+ On and off in seconds
+ No residue, no risk to paint
+ Reusable event after event
+ Perfect if your track car is also your daily
- More expensive upfront
- Can shift at very high speeds if not thick enough
- Won't stick to carbon fiber or fiberglass

Our take: if it's a dedicated track car, vinyl is the way to go. If you're dailying it, magnetics pay for themselves in convenience.

We make both. https://blueridgecustomco.com/racing-packages.html

posts.text:
Rally decal requirements aren't the same across sanctioning bodies. Here's a quick breakdown.

ARA (American Rally Association):
- Car numbers on doors, hood, roof, and rear
- Minimum 8" on doors, 12" on roof
- White numbers on dark backgrounds, black on light — no exceptions
- Blood type required for driver and co-driver
- "OK" and "NOT OK" signs must be accessible from outside
- Event-specific decals provided at registration

NASA Rally Sport:
- Similar number placement but different size minimums
- Class designation required
- More flexibility on color combinations
- Organization-specific contingency strips

The differences trip people up, especially if you run both. We can set you up with a base kit that works for both, plus org-specific add-ons.

Fellow rally driver here — I've dealt with all of this firsthand and built our kits around what actually gets you through tech without hassle.
